ledger_events.query: Inspect the three GeoPackage datasets and report available layers, geometry types, CRS/EPSG codes, feature counts, and relevant attribute fields. Identify which layer contains hospital point locations and which contains Centre County tract polygons suitable for choropleth mapping. Also check county subdivisions for possible boundary/context use.

Retrieve and inspect the hospital and county subdivision GeoPackages, and complete metadata inspection for all inputs. Report artifact paths, layer names, CRS/EPSG, geometry types, feature counts, and fields for fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg and fx_county_subdivisions_utm.gpkg; confirm tract metadata as well.

Retrieve the hospital dataset only. Open fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg, identify its layer, geometry type, CRS, feature count, and fields, and return the retrieved artifact path. Do not retrieve the tract or subdivision datasets again.

Please locate the input files by exact filename in the provided data workspace and retrieve fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg specifically. The previous responses returned the tract file instead. Return the hospital GeoPackage artifact path, layer name, geometry type, CRS, feature count, and fields. If the exact file is unavailable, explicitly report that rather than returning the tract dataset.

Create the requested hospital-count choropleth using the supplied input datasets. Use fx_tracts_centre_utm.gpkg as the target polygon layer and fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg as the hospital point layer; spatially join/count hospital points within each tract, preserving tracts with zero hospitals. Validate that both layers share a CRS or reproject as needed. Produce a GeoPackage (or equivalent vector artifact) containing tract polygons and a hospital-count field, and report the output artifact path, field name, join method, CRS, and count summary. If the hospital input cannot be accessed, report the precise missing-input issue.

Create a choropleth map of hospital counts across Centre County from the spatial-join artifact. Use the tract polygons and hospital count attribute in the provided GeoPackage; ensure all Centre County tracts are represented, including zero-count tracts if the join output contains only matched features. Use fx_county_subdivisions_utm.gpkg as boundary/context if available. Select an appropriate graduated color classification, add title, legend, north arrow/scale bar if supported, and export a map image plus the mapped vector layer. Report artifact paths and the count field used. If the join artifact lacks zero-count tracts or required fields, use the original tract layer and recompute/complete the join using the available hospital input.

ledger_events.query: Inspect the spatial-join artifact and the original datasets, then produce a complete tract-level hospital-count layer for Centre County. The prior join returned only 3 matched features, so ensure all tract polygons are retained with hospital_count=0 where no hospital point falls within a tract. Identify the actual hospital-count field and do not use an ID field as the mapped variable. If necessary, recompute the point-in-polygon count from fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg, preserving tract identifiers and CRS. Export a GeoPackage named centre_county_hospital_counts_complete.gpkg and report its artifact path, layer name, count field, tract feature count, hospital total, min/max counts, and CRS.

The previous spatial joins retained only 3 matched features, which is insufficient for a tract choropleth. Perform an explicit LEFT point-in-polygon aggregation: load every tract from fx_tracts_centre_utm.gpkg, count hospital points from fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg within/intersecting each tract, and write one output feature per tract, assigning hospital_count=0 to unmatched tracts. Do not rely on an inner spatial join. Inspect all fields and use the actual tract geometry/identifier. Export a complete GeoPackage and report the artifact path, layer, feature count, hospital_count field, total hospital count, and min/max counts.

Inspect the original tract, hospital, and latest spatial-join GeoPackages. Determine feature counts, geometry types, CRS, and all attribute fields. Verify whether the join outputs contain all tracts or only 3 matched features, and identify the actual hospital-count field (if any). Return a concise diagnostic to guide creation of a valid choropleth.

Create the final choropleth robustly from the supplied datasets. Do not map an ID field. First inspect the tract and hospital layers and determine their geometry/CRS and actual fields. Build a LEFT point-in-polygon aggregation so every tract polygon is retained and create a numeric hospital_count field, with zero for tracts without hospitals. Then render a graduated-color choropleth using hospital_count, with an appropriate legend labeled 'Number of hospitals', title 'Hospital Counts by Census Tract — Centre County', and county subdivision boundaries as context if available. Export both the complete tract count GeoPackage and a standalone HTML map. Report both artifact paths, tract count, hospital total, count range, and mapped field.
